sentences.text: The Appellants/ Claimants unsatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal have preferred this Appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

The details of compensation awarded by the Tribunal are as follows :
 Heads Awarded by the  Tribunal in Rs.
 Loss of contribution 54,60,000  (Rs.50,000  (50000 x  )=
 Rs.25,000/- + 30% =
 Rs.32,500/- x 12) =
 Rs.3,90,000/- x 14  Loss of consortium 80,000  Loss of Estate 15,000  Funeral expenses 15,000  Total 55,70,000  3.
Heard Mr.K. Varadha Kamaraj, learned couns a p p e l l a n t s / c l a i m a n t s a n d M r . B . S i v a k o l l a p p a n , l e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
second respondent / Insurance Company.
The 1st respondent has remained ex-parte both before the Tribunal as well as this Court.
4. This Court has perused and examined the impugned award as well as the materials and evidence available on record before the Tribunal.
5. The 1st appellant is the wife and the 2nd appellant is the father of the deceased (accident victim).

The adverse findings of negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle insured with the 2 nd respondent rendered by the Tribunal has attained finality as no appeal has been filed by the 2nd respondent / Insurance Company.
6. The only question that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether the appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation or not.
Based on the documents produced by the appellants / claimants, which includes the pay bill of the deceased (Ex.P18), the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.55,70,000/-.
7. The Tribunal has granted compensation to the appellants / claimants under all the heads, under which they are entitled to legally.
However, the Tribunal has erroneously deducted 50% while calculating the loss of contribution to the family.

Since the deceased has left behind two dependants viz., his wife, the 1st appellant herein and his father, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2nd appellant herein, the Tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3 rd, but has erroneously deducted half.

Excepting for this infirmity committed by the Tribunal, there is no scope for further interference by Kayalvizhi vs G. Janani on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61838625/
2 this Court with regard to the quantum of compensation.

Accordingly, the compensation payable to the appellants by the 2nd respondent / Insurance Company is reworked in the following manner :-

 Loss of consortium 80,000 80,000  Loss of Estate 15,000 15,000
Funeral expenses 15,000 15,000

In the result, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants, stands partly allowed by enhancing the compensation from https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.55,70,000/- to Rs.73,90,000/-, as indicated above.
No costs.

9. The second respondent / Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire award amount as assessed by this Court together with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of realization, less the amount, if any, already deposited to the credit of MCOP No.458 of 2019 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (III Addl. District and Sessions Court), Tiruvallur @
Poonamallee, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
